title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
summary: Karen Simonyan and Andrew Zisserman submitted 'Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition' on September 4, 2014, reporting convolutional networks pushed to 16-19 weight layers using small 3x3 convolution filters.
significance: A documented computer-vision research milestone that systematically examined increased ConvNet depth and produced the 16-layer and 19-layer models commonly associated with the VGG architecture family.
organizations: Visual Geometry Group, University of Oxford

verification.note: The original arXiv record establishes the September 4, 2014 submission date, authors, investigation of convolutional-network depth, use of very small 3x3 filters, and reported 16-19 weight-layer configurations. The University of Oxford Visual Geometry Group project page independently corroborates the authors, 16-19-layer depth, ILSVRC 2014 results, and release of the two best-performing 16-layer and 19-layer models. This record intentionally uses the arXiv submission date as the event boundary rather than treating it as an architecture-invention, competition, model-weight-release, or later ICLR publication date. No ancestry, influence, causality, or relationship to later systems is inferred.
